questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted a destination within the EU as I did not want to go too far from home and also wanted to learn more about EU Law. I love Italy ind a had been in Rome a couple of times before and loved the city. I heard that LUISS is a very good university so I ended up applying for LUISS Guido Carli in Rome.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am overall very satisfied with my study abroad experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, we got a lot of useful e-mails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a big meeting on the first day where we got a lot of useful information about our upcoming semester and so on.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: In general, LUISS staff was so helpful and good and quick at answering any questions.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find anything that was not very expensive. Luckily, a family friend of mine knew a lady that wanted to rent a room to me not too expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I loved to live in the center of Rome (which is a little far from campus) so I would highly recommend that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I said, it was not easy to find housing. But I did not look at the housing at campus because I wanted to live in the center of Rome.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you just follow the given instructions step by step it was very easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to fill in an online learning agreement and upload a photo of ourselves and of course give essential information about ourselves. We also had to chose courses but we were able to change them when we arrived at LUISS.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Good e-mails and quick responses on e-mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Just follow the instructions step by step. it might seem 
unmanageable at first, but it will all work out in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything was very good and I had a good mix of different courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were quite easy (ex. Media Law and New Technologies and Labour Law) and some were more difficult (ex. International and European Taxation

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More student involvement in UCPH and more case-based in UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Media Law
New Technologies and Labour Law
International and European Taxation
International Organizations 
EU Law before Courts: Rights and Procedures.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
International and European Taxation - very difficult but I leaned a lot. 
EU Law Before Courts - I leaned a lot and the professor was very nice.
Media Law - quite easy and no actual exam.

questions.answer: I was lucky as I did not have any unexpected costs.

questions.answer: Housing was more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dit not really use any non-academic opportunities at LUISS so I don't know.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know as I did not participate in any of these activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know as I did not participate in any of these activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a weekend trip to Bologna of Florence and take a day trip to Castel Gandolfo (40 minutes by train).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy as I have been to Italy a lot of times and the people are very nice and easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I dod not really socialize with local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the nice people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be in good time with finding housing as it can be quite difficult. 
If possible, chose courses that gives to a scheme with one day of a week (I had all of my Fridays off)
If possible, chose courses with different types of exams (the oral exams where the most demanding so I am glad I only had two of them)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improved my academic English. Personally, I developed a lot by living in a foreign country alone.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Studying in English and finding housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
